Memory is now intact and consolidated (99% full, no data lost). The growth-formula entry now carries the full three formulas plus the new PROJECT-FORWARD mechanic.

Reflection summary:

The methodology was correct — CAGR over 2001→2006 projected forward to 2011 equals V_2006²/V_2001 (since horizon = observation span). My 560682.94 vs gold 339501.88 is a 1.65x overshoot with no clean unit factor, which is the signature of a base-value mis-read, not a formula error.

What I saved (consolidated into existing memory, no skill needed):
- The PROJECT-FORWARD shortcut: when the projection horizon equals the observation span, V_C = V_B²/V_A.
- The key amplification insight: in a squared projection, mis-reading the small early base massively amplifies the error. Series I bonds were tiny in Mar 2001 (launched Sep 1998), so any base mis-read (or grabbing the all-savings-bond total instead of the Series-I-only row) produces a large overshoot — exactly the ~1.65x pattern seen here.

This is generalizable to all "grow at observed rate, project forward" Treasury Bulletin questions and reinforces the existing "read exact series" trap. No new standalone skill warranted — the existing officeqa-treasury-bulletin skill already covers growth formulas and value-reading traps; this nuance belongs as a compact diagnostic in memory.
